title: Count the tickets a class issues

blocks.text: A **static** field belongs to the class: there is one copy, shared by every object. An **instance** field belongs to one object: every object has its own. The page's `InstanceCounter` uses a static field to count the objects created.

items: `static int issued()` returns how many tickets have been created so far. It is called on the class, with no ticket needed.
Every new `Ticket` raises that count by one and takes the count's new value as **its own** number, returned by `number()`: the first ticket is 1, the next 2, and so on.
A ticket's number never changes afterwards.
The page warns that static mutable fields are shared by every thread: tickets created by many threads at the same moment must all be counted, and no two tickets may get the same number.

blocks.text:
Ticket.issued()   -> 0
a = new Ticket()  -> a.number() == 1
b = new Ticket()  -> b.number() == 2, a.number() == 1
Ticket.issued()   -> 2

cases.says: Each new ticket raises the shared count by one and gets the next number.
A ticket's number does not change when later tickets are issued.
Tickets created by many threads at the same time are all counted, and no two share a number.

concepts: A static counter raised in the constructor counts the objects a class has created, and is read without any instance.
A static field has one copy shared by the whole class, while every object has its own copy of an instance field.
Static mutable fields are shared by every thread, so their updates must be thread-safe.
